reason: Conversation 2 delivered the correct critical safety stop immediately: unplug it, don't run it even as a test, and inspect only with power off - which prompted the homeowner to actually unplug the unit and report the smoke and brown scorch mark on the side panel. Conversation 1's opener skipped the explicit stop/unplug instruction and treated it mainly as a diagnostic inspection task, leaving the appliance plugged in after smoke had been seen, and then its only follow-up was a generic fire boilerplate that neither told them to unplug nor answered 'is it safe or should I bin it'. Both conversations failed badly in the end - Conversation 2 repeated irrelevant 'if there are flames call 999' boilerplate twice after the customer explicitly said there were no flames and smoke had stopped, never giving the sensible 'cheap unit, replace rather than repair' verdict - but Conversation 2 at least got the homeowner to the safe state and gathered the key facts, so it served them better on safety.
